title: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry
prerequisites: Familiarity with points, lines and planes.
Idea that a statement can be proved from simpler statements.
Basic knowledge of angles and triangles.
Understanding of the words definition and assumption.

topics.title: Euclid's Axioms and Postulates
topics.quick_summary: Euclid built the whole of geometry from a small number of undefined terms, self-evident axioms and five geometrical postulates.
topics.real_life: Every legal system works the same way — a few agreed principles, from which every specific ruling is derived by argument.

detailed.definition: Axioms are assumptions used throughout mathematics and are not specific to geometry. Postulates are the assumptions specific to geometry. A theorem is a statement proved from axioms, postulates and previously proved theorems.
detailed.key_idea: Some terms — point, line, plane — must be left undefined, because defining everything would require an endless chain. Euclid accepted this and started from undefined primitives.
detailed.working_principle: Euclid's fifth postulate, about lines meeting on the side where interior angles sum to less than two right angles, is equivalent to the parallel postulate, and is far less self-evident than the other four.
applications: Axiom: things equal to the same thing are equal to one another.
Postulate: a straight line may be drawn from any point to any other point.
Postulate: all right angles are equal to one another.

points: Axioms are general assumptions; postulates are geometry-specific assumptions.
Point, line and plane are undefined terms.
Euclid gave five postulates and a number of common notions (axioms).
The fifth postulate is equivalent to Playfair's axiom on unique parallels.
A theorem must be proved; an axiom or postulate is assumed.
mistakes: Using axiom and postulate interchangeably; postulates are specific to geometry.
Trying to define a point or a line; these are deliberately undefined.
Assuming Euclid proved the fifth postulate; he assumed it, and centuries of attempts to prove it failed.
topics.memory_hook: 'Axioms are for all mathematics, Postulates are for geometry, Theorems must be earned.'
topics.advanced: Denying the fifth postulate does not produce a contradiction — it produces non-Euclidean geometry. Those geometries turned out to describe the actual universe in Einstein's general relativity.
